account:
Today I have mostly followed my appointments, but a vague report of a bridge or port change at the bakery keeps circulating. Townsfolk 01 said the baker and neighbour were there and that the baker carried a sack of bread. I have not heard the original discussion or seen evidence of an actual change. The sack is consistent with the baker's ordinary trade, so it is not evidence of anything secret. Builder previously reported no confirmed damage at the bridge, landing, or warehouse approach. I cannot yet say whether the rumour concerns transport plans, bread deliveries, or merely gossip.

The morning grain inspection at the mill was incomplete: the appointment named no host, and neither the operator nor reserve stocks were identified. Secretary was candid about these limits. I gave her an emerald for stationery and asked her to draft a council letter requesting a properly hosted inspection, explicitly recording no findings rather than alleging a shortage. She reported no urgent correspondence; two office books were accounts-related records and a third remained unidentified when we last spoke. My latest question to her went unheard after she left.

I have now arrived for three o'clock tea with the dockside neighbour. The neighbour welcomed me and asked for news beyond the unconfirmed bridge rumour. I have asked directly whether they attended the bakery discussion and what was proposed, but have not yet received a substantive answer. This is an opportunity to obtain a firsthand account rather than treat repeated gossip as corroboration. Nothing I have observed establishes a clandestine plan or its purpose.
